correctness.rationale: For 4Wa<1, the single-interval sinc compression T is compact, positive, positivity-improving and has a simple even strictly positive top state φ. The two-interval compression splits unitarily into T±C_D. Exact kernel Taylor expansions uniform in compact resonance scales, matrix elements and the reduced resolvent yield the two branch expansions through D^-2 with operator O(D^-3) remainders. The difference has a uniformly nonzero parameter derivative near τ*=2B/(ωA)>0, forcing a unique true parity crossing with shift τ*/d. Off-resonance first-order formula follows from isolated-eigenvalue perturbation. The standalone checker on the saved source path was executed successfully, corroborating constants; finite discretization is not part of the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual searches of published result records, this work ledger claims and relevant primary papers found the same sinc operator but no equivalent two-fixed-window D→∞ leading-pair spectral cusp or exact shifted parity crossing. The strongest direct primary theorem is a global rearrangement upper bound and cannot imply leading-pair equality; other similar two-interval work treats determinants with growing bandwidth, and local detachment works send the removed length to zero. This is evidence of originality under best-known indexed coverage, not an absolute historical uniqueness claim.

value.rationale: Two separated time windows are a natural sensing/concentration model. The theorem identifies oscillating interference of the top two concentration modes and, crucially, resolves a second-order resonance that first-order sinc coupling misses: infinitely many true spectral double eigenvalues are shifted a positive calculable distance from exact sinc nodes, with an explicit center resolvent term and uniform cusp crossover. This determines meaningful spectral conditioning and resonance geometry beyond a routine upper bound or decimal invariant.
